claim: If G is finitely generated and w is a nonidentity element killed by every homomorphism from G to every sofic group, then every finite-dimensional representation G -> GL_d(K) over every field K kills w.
quantifiers: For all fields K, finite dimensions d>=1, and group homomorphisms rho:G->GL_d(K), rho(w)=I.
proof: The image rho(G) is finitely generated and linear, hence residually finite by Mal'cev. If rho(w) were nonidentity, a finite quotient would separate it; composing G->rho(G)->Q contradicts the universal-sofic-kernel premise because finite groups are sofic.

supplied: universal kernel property for all homomorphisms to sofic groups
not_acquired: a validated N06/N27/N65 presentation and explicit literal w

costs.effectivity: Mal'cev residual finiteness is nonquantitative here; no quotient-size/runtime bound is claimed

strongest_baseline: The universal-kernel property directly excludes sofic approximations only under the separate N06 finite rank certificate. This theorem adds exact finite-dimensional linear representations over arbitrary fields.
falsifier: A homomorphism rho:G->GL_d(K) with rho(w) != I would falsify the theorem or one of its stated premises.

claim: For a finite presentation with a nontrivial universal-sofic-kernel word w of expanded length L, every approximate rank or unitary Hilbert-Schmidt model separating w lies at least the word-separation divided by L from every exact same-dimension representation; any linear-sofic or hyperlinear model therefore witnesses failure of stability of that presentation in its metric.
quantifiers: For every tuple A_s and every exact representation tuple B_s in the same dimension/field, max_s d(A_s,B_s)>=d(w(A),I)/L, with normalized rank distance or normalized Hilbert-Schmidt distance as appropriate.
proof: The universal-kernel theorem makes w(B)=I for every exact finite-dimensional representation. Telescoping the L letterwise factors gives d(w(A),w(B))<=L max_s d(A_s,B_s), because normalized rank and normalized Hilbert-Schmidt are invariant under the invertible/unitary left-right factors. Rearrangement gives the lower bound. A faithful metric-ultraproduct model has positive separation for w, while its finitely many presentation relators tend to identity, so it is not exactifiable with vanishing same-dimension generator error.

falsifier: A same-dimension exact representation closer than d(w(A),I)/L contradicts telescoping; an exact representation with w nonidentity contradicts the first theorem.

claim: For a field k, any group G with an injective rank-metric ultraproduct representation over that same k has k[G] stably finite.
quantifiers: For every field k and group G admitting an injective homomorphism into a rank-metric ultraproduct of GL_n(k), the group algebra k[G] is stably finite.
proof: For square matrices A,B over k, ker(I-AB) and ker(I-BA) have equal dimensions, so rank(I-AB)=rank(I-BA). This identity persists in rank ultraproducts and every finite matrix amplification, making the target stably finite. Arzhantseva-Paunescu Theorem 7.4 supplies an injective algebra extension from a fixed-field group rank embedding; injectivity then reflects direct finiteness back to k[G].

acquired: coordinate rank identity and stable-finiteness deduction

claim: Small normalized Hilbert-Schmidt error does not in general imply small normalized rank error, and no unital field map F_p -> C exists; these facts block the naive unitary/complex route to fixed-characteristic group-ring direct finiteness.
quantifiers: For every prime p, there is no unital field homomorphism F_p -> C; for U_n=e^(i/n)I_n, d_HS(U_n,I_n)->0 while normalized rank(U_n-I_n)=1 for every n.
proof: The scalar equation p*1=0 in F_p would map to p*1=0 in C, impossible. For the matrix example, U_n-I_n is a nonzero scalar multiple of I_n and has rank n; its normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm is |e^(i/n)-1|, which tends to zero.

not_acquired: any counterexample to an abstract hyperlinear-to-direct-finite theorem

strongest_baseline: The fixed-field rank theorem proves direct finiteness when rank approximations exist over the matching field. The counterexample blocks only identity-based conversion of HS-null errors into rank-null errors.
falsifier: A unital field map F_p -> C or a failure of the explicit scalar rank/norm computation would falsify this claim.

claim: A group admitting a faithful normalized-Hilbert-Schmidt ultraproduct model by monomial unitary matrices with phases in one fixed finite cyclic group is sofic.
quantifiers: Fix k>=1. For every finite F and tolerance eta>0, an injective HS-ultraproduct homomorphism into monomial U(D) matrices over mu_k admits a finite permutation (F,eta)-approximation on a lifted set of size kD followed by a finite m-fold product.
proof: Lift each monomial Ue_j=omega^{a(j)}e_{sigma(j)} to the permutation Pi_k(U)(j,s)=(sigma(j),s+a(j)) on [D]xZ/k. The lift is a homomorphism. Columnwise phase gap c_k=min{2,4sin^2(pi/k)} gives d_H(Pi(U),Pi(V))<=||U-V||_2^2/c_k and ||U-I||_2^2<=4d_H(Pi(U),id). For finite F, faithfulness gives a positive minimum HS separation gamma_F>0 among distinct elements in the ultraproduct; a coordinate stage separates each pair by at least gamma_F/2, hence the lifts by at least gamma_F^2/16. An m-fold product makes fixed-point fraction at most (1-gamma_F^2/16)^m. If relation HS errors are e, lifted Hamming defects are at most e^2/c_k and the product defects at most m e^2/c_k. Choose m and then e to meet eta. This yields a sofic approximation.

supplied: faithful HS-ultraproduct embedding into monomial unitary matrices with one fixed phase group mu_k
acquired: finite-product amplification and explicit tolerance conditions
not_acquired: a fixed-phase monomial model of the actual N06/N27/N65 candidate

strongest_baseline: Sofic implies hyperlinear through permutation matrices. This proves the converse only for a fixed finite-phase monomial subclass; unrestricted hyperlinearity remains open.
falsifier: A fixed-k faithful monomial HS-ultraproduct embedding of a group proven nonsofic would contradict the explicit finite rounding theorem; a failure of either columnwise inequality would contradict its direct calculation.
